advertisements.description:
One account states that the name Titay comes from the word “Taytay,” a Subanen and Visayan word meaning bridge.

One version of our history suggests that the Subanens and Kalibugans were among the original inhabitants of the area known as Taytay, referring to the bridges found along their homes and communities. Over time, the name evolved and came to be known as Titay.

Inspired by this story, the arch of Taytay Market takes the form of a bridge; a symbol of connection, heritage, and community.

Welcome to Taytay Market, a bridge that connects Titayanons. A place where our history meets the present, and where every Titayanon comes together.

𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘 𝐌𝐄𝐃𝐈𝐂𝐀𝐋 𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐏𝐎𝐍𝐒𝐄 (𝐕𝐄𝐇𝐈𝐂𝐔𝐋𝐀𝐑 𝐀𝐂𝐂𝐈𝐃𝐄𝐍𝐓)

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) Shift A personnel responded to a vehicular accident at Barangay Kitabog, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay, to provide the necessary emergency medical assistance.  
       
        Upon arrival at the scene, the responding team secured the area and conducted an immediate primary assessment. One female patient was found sitting on a chair at the roadside, conscious and oriented following a vehicular crash. Upon assessment, abrasion was noted on the right knee, tenderness on the left hip and abrasion on the left dorsal foot.  

        Immediate first aid was rendered by irrigating the wound with an appropriate cleansing solution, followed by the application of povidone-iodine (Betadine) to the affected area to help prevent infection.  The patient's condition was continuously monitored, including vital signs and overall clinical status, until her condition stabilized.  Medical transport to the nearest appropriate health facility for further evaluation and treatment was offered; however, the patient refused transport after being informed of the potential risks associated with declining medical care.
        
        A Refusal of Transport waiver was explained, signed, and properly secured. The patient was left at the scene in stable condition and was advised to seek immediate medical attention if symptoms persisted, worsened, or new symptoms developed.  

𝐈𝐍 𝐂𝐀𝐒𝐄 𝐎𝐅 𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘, call 911 or contact the Titay MFS Hotline Number: 0965-509-0944.

🔥 INDUSTRIAL & HAZARDOUS MATERIALS MONTH 2026 🔥

ALAMIN. IWASAN. AGAPAN. KALIGTASAN, UNAHIN!

Sa industriya, bawat kemikal, kagamitan, at proseso ay may kaakibat na panganib. Kaya naman, **safety first bago trabaho!

🧪 TIP #1: ALAMIN ANG HAZARD!
Bago magsimula, kilalanin ang mga hazardous materials sa inyong lugar. Basahin ang labels, warning signs, at Safety Data Sheet (SDS) upang malaman ang tamang paghawak at pag-iimbak.

🔥 TIP #2: IWAS SPARK, IWAS SUNOG!
Ilayo ang apoy, spark, sigarilyo, at iba pang ignition sources sa flammable materials. Tiyaking ligtas ang lugar bago magsagawa ng welding, cutting, o grinding.

Tandaan: Isang simpleng pag-iingat ngayon ay maaaring makaiwas sa malaking sunog at pagkawala ng buhay at ari-arian. 💪🧯

Ligtas na trabaho, ligtas na komunidad!
Para sa fire safety concerns, makipag-ugnayan sa **Titay Municipal Fire Station.**

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) Shift A personnel promptly responded to a reported vehicular accident at Barangay Kitabog, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay, where an adult male patient was found conscious and responsive with a visible deformity of the left distal tibia and fibula and a laceration on the left thigh.

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) Shift A personnel received a report regarding a vehicular accident at Barangay Palomoc, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay.

Upon receipt of the report, the responding team immediately proceeded to the scene to provide the necessary emergency medical assistance.

Upon arrival, the responding team secured the area and conducted an immediate primary assessment. An adult male patient was found unconscious and unresponsive following the vehicular crash. Initial assessment revealed signs consistent with blunt head trauma, including contusion and swelling around the left orbital area and an avulsion wound on the left frontal region.

Immediate first aid was rendered by applying direct pressure to the frontal wound to help control bleeding, followed by securing the dressing with an elastic bandage. High-flow oxygen was administered via a non-rebreather mask at 15 liters per minute. The patient's condition and vital signs were continuously monitored.

Vital signs were assessed and recorded as follows: BP 100/70 mmHg, PR 70 bpm, RR 20 cpm, SpO₂ 92%, and temperature 36.1°C, with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 5.

Due to the patient's critical condition, he was immediately transported via BFP Ambulance to Dr. George T. Hofer Medical Center, Tenan, Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay, for definitive medical evaluation and management.

Upon arrival at the medical facility, the patient was safely transferred and properly endorsed to the physician on duty for continuity of care.

𝐈𝐍 𝐂𝐀𝐒𝐄 𝐎𝐅 𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘, call 911 or contact the Titay MFS Hotline Number: 0965-509-0944.

The activity equipped young leaders with essential knowledge and practical skills in fire prevention, basic firefighting, rescue, first aid, and Exit Drill in the Home (EDITH), empowering them to become active advocates of safety and preparedness in their schools, homes, and communities.

The activity aimed to strengthen the knowledge, skills, and preparedness of student leaders in preventing and responding to fire and other emergencies. It provided participants with practical lessons and demonstrations on basic firefighting, rescue techniques, first aid, and Exit Drill in the Home (EDITH).

Adding an interactive approach to fire safety education, BFP Titay also facilitated online fire safety games, allowing participants to test and reinforce their knowledge through engaging and interactive activities.

The Fire Square Roadshow emphasized the important role of students as fire safety advocates and responsible members of the community. By equipping young leaders with essential fire safety knowledge and emergency response skills, the BFP seeks to help build a culture of preparedness and strengthen community resilience.

At this magnitude, no damage and aftershocks are expected.

✅ Stay calm and avoid spreading unverified information.
✅ Familiarize yourself with safe evacuation areas and emergency exits.
✅ Prepare and maintain your emergency go bag.
✅ During strong earthquakes, remember: DROP, COVER, and HOLD ON.
